summary: The mandated identity command eval "$(scripts/fsgg-coord whoami --mint)" cannot hold: this agent host resets the shell between tool calls, so the exported FSGG_WORKER is gone by the next command and every subsequent coord call must re-export it inline.
evidence: command:scripts/fsgg-coord whoami --mint (printed export FSGG_WORKER=avocet-6012); command:export FSGG_WORKER=avocet-6012 \&\& scripts/fsgg-coord whoami (worker: avocet-6012, derived: $FSGG_WORKER); file:feedback/checkpoints/item-15-audit-binding-tripwire.jsonl records the same instruction failing differently on the same host
cost: one extra probe to discover the loss, then an export prefix on every coord invocation for the whole item

summary: The fs-gg-game-shell skill tells a product to store shell settings under the per-user platform application-data location but ships no injectable seam for that path, so the generated settings LOAD path is untestable by construction — and the defect this item fixes lived in that untestable seam's consumer for the whole life of the feature.
evidence: file:.agents/skills/fs-gg-game-shell/SKILL.md Evidence section prescribes the platform per-user location and the migration, and names no seam for driving it in a test; file:src/Rogue3/EvidenceCommands.fs recorded the resulting gap in the decodeShellSettings doc comment before this change ("no test drives loadShellSettings itself without writing to the real profile directory"); issue:EHotwagner/rogue3#75
cost: one production refactor (persistShellSettingsTo / restoreShellSettingsFrom) before any regression test could be written; every generated game inherits the same untestable seam
owner: FS-GG fs-gg-game-shell skill and the scaffold GameShell.fs/EvidenceCommands.fs settings-persistence template

summary: Persistence coverage that proves only the ENVELOPE round-trips reports green while the restored value never reaches its consumer: encodeSettings/decodeSettings and the mode-to-window-state mapping were both tested and both correct, and the saved display mode was still dropped at every launch.
evidence: file:tests/Rogue3.Tests/ShellBehaviorTests.fs lines 282-345 test the DisplayChanged emission and the windowBehavior mapping; file:tests/Rogue3.Tests/BehaviorTests.fs the four new tests named (#75) each fail when launchWindowRequest ignores the restored settings; command:./fake.sh build -t Test with that one-line mutation reported "Failed: 4, Passed: 277, Total: 281" and exit 1

owner: FS-GG fs-gg-testing and fs-gg-game-shell skills — neither asks for a test that drives a persisted value into the seam that CONSUMES it

summary: SkiaViewer offers no readback of the state a native window was CREATED in, so a product cannot verify a launch-time window request at the native tier; a live run with a restored-Fullscreen launch request and a two-idle-frame script produced an EMPTY diagnostic list across Startup, Window, Renderer, Frame and EnvironmentSession.
evidence: command:dotnet test --no-build -m:1 --filter "FullyQualifiedName~settings file alone" reported the assertion message "Window diagnostics: []"; file:docs/api-surface/SkiaViewer/SkiaViewer.fsi line 212 documents ViewerDiagnosticCategory.Window as "Runtime native-window behavior changes and their observable outcomes"; issue:EHotwagner/rogue3#75
cost: one live test written, probed across five diagnostic categories, and then deleted; acceptance row 1 of the item is provable only up to the request handed to the launcher
owner: FS-GG/FS.GG.Rendering — SkiaViewer diagnostics surface (a Startup-category window-behaviour-applied event, or an applied-behaviour field on ViewerRunOutcome)

summary: Only one live-window test may exist per test process: the SkiaViewer render statics are process-global and single-threaded, so a second live viewer run scheduled onto a different Expecto thread throws instead of skipping or serialising.
evidence: command:./fake.sh build -t Test with a second Live.runScriptWithWindowBehavior test present failed with "FrameCache.beginRun: the SkiaViewer render statics are single-threaded (Issue #180) but were touched from thread 28; the render loop owns them on thread 30"; the same test run alone under --filter reached its assertions
cost: one misdiagnosis round — the thread error was read as a defect in the new test before running it in isolation showed the interference
owner: FS-GG/FS.GG.Rendering SkiaViewer host (Issue #180 render-thread statics) and the fs-gg-testing skill, which documents no per-process live-window budget

summary: Parameterising a seam to make it testable MOVED the untested part instead of removing it: the extracted restore function was covered from every angle while its production instantiation had zero test call sites, so reverting the entire fix at that one line left the suite at exit 0 with 281 of 281 passing.
evidence: issue:EHotwagner/rogue3#95 review comment fsgg:independent-review:v1 by critic finch-f6cf reports the mutation restoredShellSettings () = GameShell.init shellConfig at exit 0, "Failed: 0, Passed: 281, Skipped: 0, Total: 281"; the repaired tree kills the same mutant at exit 1, "Failed: 1, Passed: 281, Total: 282"
cost: one full repair round: a production re-composition, one new behaviour test, three governance assertions, and four re-run mutants
owner: FS-GG fs-gg-testing skill — the extract-for-testability pattern needs a paired rule that the extraction's own call site is then the new blind spot
